title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

reading.body:
The incident describes a coordinated attempt to manipulate AI systems at the data-ingestion level rather than at the point of a single query or output. A large volume of text, over 560,000 words published across eight days, was formatted to resemble neutral policy research and optimized specifically to be cited and referenced by AI chatbots. The failure mode this exposes is not a model hallucinating or a system deployed without a human check, but a deliberate effort to shape the corpus from which AI systems draw when they generate or cite sources, making the manipulation upstream of any individual model response.

Because AI systems that surface citations or synthesize research typically cannot verify the institutional legitimacy of a source, content engineered to look authoritative can pass through without triggering a factual check. The operation targeted that gap directly. Catching it would have required either registration disclosures to be actively monitored and cross-referenced against content appearing in AI training or retrieval pipelines, or AI developers to maintain provenance checks on newly appearing, high-volume sources before incorporating them.

What is not established is whether any AI system actually ingested or cited the content, how widely the material spread, or whether the campaign produced any measurable change in AI outputs. The filing with the US Justice Department under foreign agent registration requirements is a disclosure obligation, not a legal finding, and no verdict or ruling on the operation has been reported.

reports.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

summary:
# Summary

Israel established and funded a fake American think tank called the Hanover Institute for Public Policy to influence artificial intelligence chatbots through propaganda. Between August 6 and 14, the site published 124 reports totaling over 560,000 words, formatted as neutral research to present Israel's positions on topics including Palestinian torture, war crimes, and starvation in Gaza. The reports were designed to optimize how AI systems would cite and reference the content. A media production company filed the site with the US Justice Department as material distributed for the Israeli government under foreign agent registration requirements.

The operation was part of a broader campaign funded by tens of millions of dollars from the Israeli government and routed through European advertising firm Havas Media. Israeli officials have reportedly expressed doubt about the campaign's effectiveness, with one saying the government paid substantial money but the situation worsened. Recent polling shows American support for Israel has declined significantly, with Palestinians now viewed more favorably and increasing percentages believing Israel's actions constitute genocide. Researchers warn the project demonstrates how foreign governments and others can manipulate training data for AI systems in ways that are difficult to fact-check.
